name: Warm Purple
lede: Warm Purple is a vivid, reddish purple from the xkcd color survey of 2010, built by stacking the modifier "warm" onto the base color [[purple]].

sections.title: A modifier, not a story
sections.body:
The name follows the same grammar as other crowd-survey names in our data: "warm" plus the base word [[purple]], rather than a plant, mineral or place [1]. Our computed nearest ISCC-NBS block is 236, vivid reddish purple, which fits the "warm" in the name: it leans toward red [1]. Our library files Warm Purple as an alternate name of [[hyacinth-violet|Hyacinth Violet]], 4.8 units away, a Ridgway color [1].

Its closest measured look-alike is [[deep-magenta|Deep Magenta]], 3.7 units off and more vivid, the same swatch the survey also named Barney Purple [1]. [[plum|Plum]] sits further out at 5.4 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds a color within six units of this one over at least five percent of its canvas, as photographed [2]. A 2010 crowd-survey name has no particular reason to match an older painter's palette, and our archive sums up each painting in 24 colors, which pulls small vivid areas toward their neighbors [2].
